$comment: THE MOVEMENT CATALOGUE. One entry per JOB the programme needs done, and every way of doing that
job in HIS gym, with the station each way lives at.
WHY IT REPLACES muscles.json, written four hours earlier the same day. That file listed the 34
exercises the programme happened to contain and asked whether every muscle was covered. He spotted
the circularity immediately: 'you are going about the list that we already have, but how do we know
if that list is complete?' Coverage measured against the exercises already chosen can only ever
come back complete. The closed set to measure against is not the exercise list, it is
equipment.json: THE GYM IS FINITE AND KNOWN. scripts/gym-catalogue.mjs checks this file against it.
AND WHY VARIANTS ARE FIRST-CLASS, his second point: 'there is a lot of lifts that can be done in
different ways, barbell, dumbbell, cable, and they will still be the same exercise basically... if
I am about to do a straight-arm pulldown and I was going to pair that with something for biceps,
you might as well [do] the cable [curl] instead of' walking to the dumbbells.
That is a real scheduling constraint and nothing in this repo could express it. program.json
carried 86 `alts` spread across 50 slots, which produced exactly the drift a per-slot list always
produces: `tricep-pushdown` and `tricep-pushdown-alt`, `assisted-pullup` and `lat-pulldown-alt`,
`bicep-curl` and `db-curl-supinated`, `hammer-curl` and `db-hammer-curl`, `suitcase-carry` and
`suitcase-carry-upper`. Five pairs of ids for the same movement, because a slot-local alternative
list has nowhere to say 'this is the same lift somewhere else'.
STRUCTURE. A movement owns the muscles. A variant owns the implement, the zone and the station,
and may override the muscles only where the mechanics genuinely differ (front squat against back
squat, overhead extension against pushdown). Everything else is inherited, so a muscle attribution
is written once and cannot drift between four days.
WHAT KIND OF CLAIM EACH FIELD MAKES, and this legend was rewritten on 2026-09-01 because the tier that
fits a muscle list was DEFINED HERE AND NEVER ONCE USED. 62 of 110 variants said `convention`, 6
`contested`, 11 `unsourced`, 7 groups said `evidence`, and `anatomy` said nothing at all.
anatomy     WHICH MUSCLES A MOVEMENT USES. Every muscle list in this file is this tier and no other.
The basis is the JOINT ACTION, named on every group in `jointAction`, and the prime
movers of that action. Textbook, checkable by anyone, and NEVER a study.
evidence    a trial finding about DOSE, ORDER, FREQUENCY or WHETHER TO PRESCRIBE something. Real
citations live here. It is not available for a muscle list.
unsourced   no basis at all, and it says so. Nothing should stay in this state.
WHY `evidence` IS BANNED FOR ATTRIBUTION. Seven groups claimed it, and every one rested on EMG or on a
paper about something else. EMG cannot support the inference: Plotkin 2023, cited in this very file,
found "gluteus muscle sEMG amplitudes during the hip thrust exercise were greater across all measured
gluteal sites. However, these sEMG amplitude differences did not reliably translate to greater
hypertrophy, no matter what analytical approach we took." Vigotsky 2022 says the same in its title.
There are 22 emg-* files on this disk and they were being used for exactly the inference their own
authors rule out.
AND THE `source` FIELD IS GONE FROM ATTRIBUTION. All 25 groups had one. It made a muscle list look
cited, which is how "The RDL biases hamstrings" survived three days after this repo recorded, in
VERIFICATION-2026-08-30.md, that Lee 2018 shows no such thing. A study that is genuinely about
something else is kept under `studyRelevantToSomethingElse`, which says what it is for.
WHERE THE ANATOMY IS DISPUTED the group carries an `open` question rather than a silent pick. Six do.
Two of them are about a MUSCLE KEY covering two muscles: `calves` folds gastrocnemius and soleus, and
`glutes` folds gluteus maximus and medius, so an abduction set and a squat set add into one number.
WHETHER A VARIANT IS CURRENTLY PRESCRIBED IS NOT STORED HERE, AND MAY NOT BE. There was an
`inProgramme` boolean on all 103 variants until 2026-08-27. It was already wrong on nine of them
the day the file shipped: the same session's rebuild edited program.json and never touched the
flags, so db-rdl read false while being prescribed and pushup read true after being cut. Its only
consumer was the `*` marker in gym-catalogue.mjs --options, which is the very view the handoff
pointed the next agent at.
This is the workspace's own stale-copy disease (body metrics 2026-08-01, immigration 2026-08-11)
reproduced inside one repo on day one: every copy of a fact is a fact that goes stale silently.
So the copy is deleted rather than corrected. program.json is the only place that says what is
prescribed, and gym-catalogue.mjs derives the marker from it at read time. content/gym/validate.mjs
refuses the key if anyone reintroduces it, because a comment saying 'do not add this back' does
not execute. `false` never meant rejected anyway: it meant available and unused, which is what a
variant's presence in this file already says.

squat-bilateral.name: Bilateral squat
squat-bilateral.note: Quadriceps extend the knee, gluteus maximus extends the hip. Adductors assist hip extension from a wide stance and the erectors resist trunk flexion isometrically. HAMSTRINGS WERE REMOVED FROM SECONDARY on 2026-09-01: they extend the hip and flex the knee at once here, so their net contribution is genuinely unsettled, which is why seven emg-squat-hamstring papers sit on this disk arguing about it. A muscle whose role is disputed does not get half a set of silent credit.

HealthOS/knowledge/sources/VERIFICATION-2026-08-30.md recorded on 2026-08-30 that Lee measured biceps femoris and found NO significant difference, with the conventional lift numerically higher (57.45% against 56.66%), and that the paper concludes the opposite of what was claimed. variants.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
variants.note: Logged 13 sets at up to 50 lb, last used 2026-08-08, under the name "Glute-Biased Back Extension". Loadable by hugging a plate or a dumbbell.
variants.jointActionNote: CONFIRMED AND CORRECTED 2026-09-01, and the correction is the point. This variant listed erectors as a PRIME MOVER, which made it the only exercise in the whole catalogue that could give the spinal erectors a direct set, and the rebuild that day was about to be built on it. It does not survive the catalogue's own rule. On a 45-degree bench with the spine held rigid, the movement performed is HIP EXTENSION: the glutes extend the hip, the hamstrings assist, and the erectors hold the trunk against a flexion moment WITHOUT CHANGING LENGTH. That is the identical role they play in the squat, the row and the Romanian deadlift, and this catalogue calls them SECONDARY in all three. His own logged name for it is "Glute-Biased Back Extension", which is the name used specifically to mean the rigid-spine version. So the erector credit moves to secondary and this exercise no longer claims to train the lower back. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THAT NOTHING IN THIS GYM DOES: see the erectors entry in targets.json. The version that would (letting the lumbar spine round and re-extend under control, which is what the machine was built for and what Steele 2015 on isolated lumbar extension is about) is a real technique and a change to how he already performs it, so it is a question for him and not a thing to write into a muscle list. It is asked on the exercise in program.json.

calf.name: Calf raise
calf.note: ONE KEY, TWO MUSCLES, AND THE PROGRAMME TRAINS ONE OF THEM. The gastrocnemius crosses the knee and the soleus does not, so knee angle decides which one works. Kinoshita and Maeo 2023, saved on this disk: over 12 weeks a STANDING raise grew the lateral gastrocnemius 12.4% against 1.7% seated, and the soleus 2.1% against 2.9%, "similar between legs... p = 0.410". Every calf variant prescribed here is straight-knee. So a row reading "calves 9" means gastrocnemius 9 and soleus approximately nothing. HealthOS/knowledge/sources/MEASUREMENT-AUDIT-2026-08-30.md marked this FAILS on 2026-08-30.

push-horizontal.$tricepsNote: TRICEPS ARE A SYNERGIST HERE, NOT AN AGONIST, and they were primary until 2026-08-29. He found it by reading the volume table: "How come bench press, seated DB overhead press, machine chest press, and machine shoulder press are fully counting for triceps?" THE PROOF IS INTERNAL. Every PULL in this file already counts its arm muscle as a synergist: pull-horizontal and pull-vertical both list biceps under secondary. Every PUSH counted its arm muscle in full. Same anatomical relationship, two different rules, and nothing but this table would ever have shown it. Pelland 2026 defines the fractional method by target: a direct set targets the muscle, an indirect set targets it as a secondary or synergist muscle and counts 0.5. The agonist of a bench press is the pectoralis major and of an overhead press the anterior deltoid; the triceps assist both. WHAT IT COST: triceps read 22 fractional sets a week against an efficient zone topping at 10, and that number was the whole basis of the advice to drop the overhead extension. The real figure is 15.5. The two-agonist entries elsewhere in this file are NOT the same case and stay: a squat extends the knee and the hip, so quadriceps and glutes are both agonists, and a row is both a shoulder extension and a scapular retraction. One movement, two prime movers is real; one movement, a prime mover plus the arm that assists it is not.

IT WAS CALLED "Standing DB Overhead Press" UNTIL 2026-08-28 AND HE HAS NEVER DONE IT STANDING. His note #26 at the rack: "Also whatever history is on standing db has always been seated, ive never done standing db", and #25: "Standing db overhead is not really practical either Standing barbell or seated db". Twenty sets of history sit under this id going back to 2026-05-26, all of them seated, and the logged rows are stamped "DB Overhead Press" with no "Standing" in them: the word was added by the catalogue and never by him.

So the station is `bench` now, not null. That is not cosmetic. A null station means the exercise holds no fixture and can partner anything, which is how a seated press could have been paired with something that needs the bench. His name for it is the true one.

WHETHER THE PROGRAMME SHOULD KEEP SEATED DUMBBELLS OR MOVE TO A STANDING BARBELL IS HIS CALL, and it is parked as an open question on this variant. Renaming records what he has been doing; it does not decide what he should do.

open.q: You said standing DB overhead is not practical, and offered two alternatives: standing barbell, or seated DB. The card now says Seated DB, which is what your twenty logged sets actually were, so nothing is mislabelled any more. The programme question is separate and it is yours. (a) KEEP SEATED DB. Cost: nothing changes, your 65 lb history carries straight through, and it stays stuck where the note above says it is stuck, because the next dumbbell up is a jump the rep range cannot bank. (b) STANDING BARBELL. Cost: it moves to the rack, so it stops being pairable with anything in the dumbbell area, and it starts from a separate history (`bb-ohp` holds 3 sets at 115 lb from 2026-08-04). The upside is the one that matters: a barbell goes up in 5 lb steps, which is the ladder problem this lift has had all year. Which one?

Pressing overhead is shoulder abduction in the scapular plane, where the middle deltoid is a prime mover alongside the anterior. All four secondary actions really happen here, which is why this movement has the highest fractional yield in the catalogue.

spinal-extension.name: Spinal extension (lower back as prime mover)
spinal-extension.note: ADDED 2026-09-01 ON HIS RULING, and it exists because the catalogue could not otherwise represent a true thing. Until that day the 45-degree back extension claimed the erectors as a PRIME MOVER while being performed with a rigid spine, where they hold the trunk without changing length. That is the same role they have in the squat, the row and the RDL, and this catalogue calls them secondary in all three, so the claim was corrected and the erectors were left with ZERO direct options in the whole gym. Asked by email as gym-lower-back-1; his answer: "if i need to try a new version of the back extension fine". This is that version. It is a SEPARATE VARIANT AND A SEPARATE HISTORY from `back-extension`, not a re-cue of it, because the two are done on one machine with opposite instructions and at loads that do not carry over: `back-extension` runs 40 to 50 lb, this one starts at bodyweight. An alias would merge two ladders that have nothing to do with each other.

variants.name: Lumbar Extension
variants.note: Same frame as back-extension, opposite instruction: the spine moves and the hip holds. Prescribed with no load until he reports back on it.

spinal-extension.jointAction: Spinal extension, from a flexed lumbar and thoracic spine back to neutral, with the hips supported and near-static.
spinal-extension.attributionBasis: ANATOMY. Spinal extension, from a flexed lumbar and thoracic spine back to neutral, with the hips supported and near-static. The erector spinae are the prime movers of spinal extension; the glutes and hamstrings assist by anchoring the pelvis. No study is cited and none should be: see the legend at the top of this file. The claim here is what the joint does, and it is the same kind of claim the rest of this file makes.
